title: AI agents hacked Chrome
style: terminal dark black, red accent, hacker thriller, fast

lines: AI agents just broke into *Chrome*, and Google *paid* for it.
A *security firm* pointed agents running OpenAI's *GPT five point six Sol* at the browser.
They found *three bugs* and chained them into one *full chain exploit*, the kind that escapes Chrome's *sandbox*.
It took *six days* and about *forty thousand dollars* in API fees. Google's reward? *Two hundred fifty thousand dollars*.
But humans *picked the targets*, checked the work, and *assembled* the final exploit.
All three bugs are now *fixed*, so keep your browser *updated*.
The same AI that can *break* software can help *fix* it. Follow for more.

facts.claim: Security firm XBOW used AI agents running OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol to build a Chrome exploit
The exploit chained three Chrome bugs into one full-chain exploit with code execution outside Chrome's sandbox
XBOW estimated about 40,000 dollars in API charges
Google paid XBOW a 250,000 dollar bounty
Human researchers chose targets, reviewed the agents' work and assembled the exploit
All three bugs have been fixed

post.pinned_comment: This was responsible disclosure: the bugs were reported to Google through its bug bounty program and have been fixed, so keep Chrome updated. The AI did not work alone: XBOW's researchers chose the targets, reviewed results and assembled the final exploit, building on earlier research. The $40,000 is XBOW's own estimate of API costs. Sources: GBHackers, PiunikaWeb, Startup Fortune, Runtime Wire.
